articles.title: Indie Game Storefront Itch Deletes a 'Couple of Terabytes of AI Slop,' Adds 'No AI' Filter to Search Results
articles.summary: Itch has clamped down on the deluge of low effort generative AI games flooding its store, confirming the removal of a couple of terabytes of "AI slop."
articles.body:
Itch has clamped down on the deluge of low effort generative AI games flooding its store, confirming the removal of a couple of terabytes of "AI slop."

In a statement on social media , the indie game storefront said it had begun the process of removing thousands of AI games and other marketplace items, including asset packs for game developers, due to spam. “Just deleted a couple terabytes of AI slop,” Itch said.

"Just because you can upload 10 terabytes of poorly optimized AI generated models doesn't mean you should upload 10 terabytes of poorly optimized AI generated models," Itch continued .

Itch has also added generative AI disclosure filtering to its website, including on its search results page "in order to better control what you see." Via the 'No AI' filter, users can strip out games with AI disclosures.

When asked if this was a blanket ban on generative AI, Itch said it’s only against the site’s terms and conditions when it comes to spam. “Avoid uploading excessive amounts of automatically generated or AI-generated content,” the site’s official terms and conditions states. AI generated content is fine if it’s “clearly stated in your project description and that it adds substantial value to the user experience.” Multiple iterations of the same thing spat out with slight variations are against the rules, and AI content has to have some sense of curation to pass the store’s guidelines.

Itch has taken a stronger stance on AI than, for example, Valve. While Steam has an AI discosure policy for store pages, Valve does not limit AI-focused developer access to its platform, nor block "AI slop" from from it despite complaints from fans and developers about the deluge of low effort games that flooded the recent Steam Next Fest . Valve also put the onus on developers to ensure their game stands out amid the detritus. In particular, there’s been a big issue on Steam of developers having their games instantly cloned with AI as soon as they share any development progress.

"Rather than relying on a single mechanic that someone can easily copy, you need to keep growing your game by adding features, personality, and creativity that stem from your own perspective," Valve’s Tom Giardino said.

Epic Games, on the other hand, is all-in on AI. Its boss, Tim Sweeney, has heavily criticized Valve for its AI disclosure policy , calling it a "political act."

articles.title: Nintendo Reveals the Changes It Made to The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time's Notoriously Difficult Water Temple for the Remake
articles.summary: Nintendo has discussed the changes it has made to the notoriously difficult Water Temple for The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake.
articles.body:
Nintendo has discussed the changes it has made to the notoriously difficult Water Temple for The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake.

In an interview with Zelda boss Eiji Aonuma, Production Group No.3’s HokWai Ng, and other members of the development team published on the Nintendo website , changes made to dungeons were outlined. Crucially, Aonuma — who worked on the original Ocarina of Time back in the ‘90s — was able to finally get to what he called “overdue homework” on the Water Temple.

The original Water Temple in the 1998 N64 masterpiece is infamous for its complex puzzle solving, but also its lack of handholding. This made it a bewildering challenge for many players of the original game. As someone who played Ocarina of Time back in the day — and without the help of a guide — I found the Water Temple pretty frustrating. It took me longer to work out than pretty much any part of the game, as I struggled to make sense of the water levels and locked doors. And don’t get me started on that item toggling.

Ng said that Nintendo’s approach with the remake was to retain the dungeon mechanisms from the original game, but improve “playability.”

“For example, we placed objects in such a way that players intuitively figure out which direction to go,” he said. “So if you look closely, you may notice areas where the layout differs slightly from the original game.”

For Aonuma, the Water Temple was personal. “I wanted to do something about the Water Temple I created 28 years ago,” he said, laughing. “Since it became well known for its difficulty in the original game, I had the team make some adjustments in this version. When I designed the Water Temple all those years ago, I wanted to create an experience where simply being underwater was fun. It was a time when there were very few 3D games that even let players go underwater. I enjoy freediving, and what I find fascinating about being underwater is how different everything feels. The sounds change, and it feels like you’re in a completely different space. I wanted to create a place where players could experience those sensations.

“However, with the dungeon’s complex structure and a lot of item toggling involved, you often had to open the menu screen repeatedly, making it hard to keep track of where you were and which way you were facing. We addressed those issues in this version.”

To that end, the remake makes item toggling “much easier,” and Nintendo has “changed some of the walls that made it easy to lose your sense of direction to lattice-style structures, making it possible to see the rooms beyond them and get a better sense of the overall space.”

Essentially, rather than simply changing the structure to make things easier, Nintendo came up with various ideas to rework it so that players wouldn’t get lost.

As IGN’s Logan Plant spotted while viewing Ocarina of Time remake gameplay , the 3DS version’s wall lights, which helped guide players to water-shifting spots, return for the Switch 2 remake. And, as teased by Nintendo today, Link can instantly take off his iron boots without having to pause and go to the equipment menu.

There’s a fun exchange at the end of the interview that taps into the immense nostalgia fans have for Ocarina of Time, and what I imagine will be a typical household experience when the remake comes out.

“More than anything, I personally would be happy if it became a conversation starter that encourages players of different generations to share memories with each other,” Ng said. “You know, your Dad got stuck in the Water Temple plenty of times back in the day [laughs].”

Aonuma: “Then kids playing this version might say, ‘Come on, it’s not that hard.’ Poor old Dad might end up feeling deflated.”

While you wait for the game to come out, check out a special episode of Nintendo Voice Chat where we dive deeper into our Zelda preview. Meanwhile, we finally have confirmation of who actually developed the Ocarina of Time remake , and a roundup of the Ocarina of Time remake global release times .

articles.summary: Bethesda Game Studios has officially announced the subtitle for The Elder Scrolls 6. The long-awaited follow-up to Skyrim will be called Sentinel, making its official title The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel. A logo has also been revealed. Both come as part of a video message from longtime franchise director Todd Howard as Bethesda celebrates its 40th anniversary.
articles.body:
Bethesda Game Studios has officially announced the subtitle for The Elder Scrolls 6. The long-awaited follow-up to Skyrim will be called Sentinel, making its official title The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel. A logo has also been revealed. Both come as part of a video message from longtime franchise director Todd Howard as Bethesda celebrates its 40th anniversary.

The confirmation follows a report from last week that has proven to be quite correct. Xbox CEO Asha Sharma got a demo of The Elder Scrolls VI earlier this summer, and teased the subtitle in her post by replacing the name we now know to be Sentinel with eight asterisks. Turns out those asterisks were very specific then, as Sentinel is of course eight letters.

Sentinel is a city within the province of Hammerfell on the continent of Tamriel, where The Elder Scrolls is set. It sits on the northwest coast, nestled beside Iliac Bay. Hammerfell, meanwhile, is located due west of Cyrodiil, where Oblivion took place, and southwest of Skyrim (speaking of which, Bethesda notes that The Elder Scrolls 5 is "still Bethesda Game Studios’ most played game" – and we clarified with Bethesda that this is referring to total lifetime players). Its northern border is shared with the province of High Rock, and its western edge meets the Abacean Sea.

It's been a long wait for The Elder Scrolls 6, as it was first announced way back in 2018 , and fans have waited for more information on it ever since. Today's subtitle and logo reveal are the first real bits of news on it in quite some time, though we likely have at least a couple more years to wait before playing it. On Xbox and PC, that is. With Sharma's renewed focus on console exclusives , will The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel even see the light of day on a PlayStation console? That remains to be seen, but it's the biggest card Microsoft has to play in order to get more people back into its ecosystem.

For now, though, at least we've got the Sentinel name, and we'll have to cross our fingers that we get a proper reveal at next year's Xbox Showcase in June. Here's the full 40th anniversary studio walkthrough with Howard:

articles.title: World of Warcraft Forever Launch Patch Notes Bring Controller Support and Massive Class Changes
articles.summary: World of Warcraft Forever is just a day away, and now that the beta has concluded Blizzard has released its patch notes for the release build of the game. Check out all the changes.
articles.body:
World of Warcraft Forever is just a day away, and now that the beta has concluded Blizzard has released its patch notes for the release build of the game.

A bulk of the patch notes focus on class changes where, among other things, Blizzard rolled back some Shaman abilities like Lava Burst to focus the Elemental spec identity on lightning ability. And that's just one of dozens of class changes. Blizzard's goal with these class changes was to distill Forever's combat into its own identity. According to the developer notes, "some of this round of changes reflects areas where we were likely hasty in turning to Burning Crusade- or Wrath-era solutions rather than carving out new ones that better fit into the Forever combat model."

This will likely be the only major class tuning that Blizzard is going to touch before raids open next month, which is perfectly in line with how the company typically launches WoW games and expansions. The developers want to gather data on how people are playing before it changes how anything is balanced, which only makes sense.

However, Blizzard will still tweak classes to fix bugs, according to the developer notes. "With the exception of bugs and serious outliers, we don’t plan on making big tuning changes between now and the opening of the raids next month," the developer said. "Once we have sufficient data from players leveling past 30 and engaging in a wide range of content, we expect that we will do a large tuning pass based on our data."

But apart from the mass of class changes, World of Warcraft Forever's controller support has "entered a complete functional state," and gamepads can now be used in every facet of the MMO. Xbox even put out its own blog post talking about Forever's controller support , claiming that it "reimagines the way we play." WoW Forever's beta supported controllers, but that support was only in an alpha stage, and had its own limitations and bugs. Hopefully this "complete functional state" means Blizzard has figured those issues out.

I, for one, plan to download WoW Forever on an Xbox Ally X , so that I can grind while I watch TV. But because Forever's controller UI looks so similar to Final Fantasy XIV's controller interface, I can't help but wonder if this controller support is just a precursor for a full Xbox Series X release. We'll just have to wait and see what happens there.

Finally, the patch notes do detail some nerfs coming to racial abilities. Dwarves and Orcs both straight up had one of their passive abilities removed from the game, while many other races had their passives nerfed. For instance, Humans' Ruthless ability now increases critical strike chance by 1%, rather than 2%. But, hey, at least Trolls get a longer duration on Berserking – their mini-bloodlust.

Only time will tell how balance is going to fall in WoW Forever, but we won't have to wait long to see how it plays out. World of Warcraft Forever comes out tomorrow, November 4, at 3pm PST / 6pm EST , and if the beta was any indication, a lot of people are going to rush in to really push WoW's servers to their breaking point. And I'll be right there to watch it happen.

World of Warcraft Forever launch patch notes:

Throw will now correctly use the 0.5 second windup timer (was incorrectly using the throwing weapon’s attack speed).

Legacy Reward - Replica Ironforge Air Rifle can now correctly be used on allies that also have one equipped. Duration of the quitter debuff reduced to 40 seconds (was 5 minutes). Duration of the stun reduced to 2.5 seconds (was 3 seconds).

Developer’s notes: Over the course of Beta, we came to the realization that trying to hold ourselves roughly to Classic power budgets for each class meant that every new element we added needed to come at the expense of something else. Those reductions left some iconic abilities feeling lackluster, and closed the door to other potentially exciting design options. So over the last two weeks, we’ve raised damage on classes across the game, and have increased the health of higher level creatures to compensate. This additional “headroom” has allowed us to tune things to a place that we hope feels better overall. Beyond that, some of this round of changes reflects areas where we were likely hasty in turning to Burning Crusade- or Wrath-era solutions rather than carving out new ones that better fit into the Forever combat model. Our aim in class design is not perfect numerical equality, but rather for every class to feel valuable to the groups they join, with powerful, unforgettable moments brought on by mastering them. In Forever this is accomplished by doubling down on the strengths and differences that make each class unique, rather than overly unifying them.

articles.title: The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel Finally Got Its Name Today, but Bethesda Says It Will Be 'Some Time Before We’re Ready to Share More'
articles.summary: Bethesda finally revealed the name for The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel, more than eight years after teasing it at E3 2018, but we'll reportedly have to wait at least two more years before it comes out.
articles.body:
Bethesda finally revealed the name for The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel, more than eight years after teasing it at E3 2018 , but we'll reportedly have to wait at least two more years before it comes out.

After releasing its 'Official Name Reveal' trailer for The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel, Bethesda posted on X / Twitter to say that "Development continues, and while it’ll be some time before we’re ready to share more, it feels great to finally reveal the name and location with you."

So, if you were hoping that Bethesda breaking its silence was a sign that the game was coming out any time soon, well, you're going to have to wait a bit longer.

What's taking so long? Perhaps the better question is, why did Bethesda announced The Elder Scrolls 6 so early? Bloomberg's Jason Schreier posted on Bluesky to say that when Bethesda teased The Elder Scrolls 6 back in 2018, it was to "to soften the blow of Fallout 76," rather than to suggest it was anywhere close to release. The multiplayer-focused Fallout 76 was panned by critics at launch, with most Bethesda fans expressing their dismay that the studio had veered away from its single-player roots. Schreier followed up to say that The Elder Scrolls 6 is "still more than two years away!"

However, both Bethesda and Xbox CEO Asha Sharma have confirmed The Elder Scrolls 6 is in a playable state. In August, Sharma tweeted that she was getting a live playthrough of the game, while also teasing the subtitle with a lot of asterisks, which sent Elder Scrolls fans into a frenzy trying to figure out what the game would be called.

articles.title: Xbox’s smallest-ever controller is surprisingly comfortable
articles.summary: The Nano controller is designed for young people, anyone with smaller hands, and gaming on the go.
articles.body: Even though I knew Microsoft’s new Xbox Nano controller was tiny, I still gasped when I unboxed it a few days ago. The compact controller is small enough to slip into a pocket unnoticed, and it has been designed specifically for younger people, or for anyone with smaller hands. I’m not young, but I do have small hands, and I’ve been surprised at how comfortable the Nano is during gaming sessions. At just over 5 inches long, almost everything on this controller has been shrunk down somehow. The ABXY buttons are ever so slightly smaller than a regular Xbox controller, and the thumbsticks feel like miniature versions. Microsoft hasn’t changed the D-pad, though, or the size of the glowing Xbox button at the center of the controller. The big difference I noticed with the Nano over a regular Xbox controller was the size of the triggers. While they are fully analog and pressure sensitive, they have more of a click when you bottom them out compared with the thud on a bigger Xbox controller. They’re noticeably smaller, as you’d expect, and the bumper buttons above the triggers feel less clicky than the regular ones. I thought the Nano controller would feel awkward after a few hours of gaming, but the grips really help with comfort levels — a lot of smaller controllers sacrifice grips to keep the controller thin and lightweight. It does mean the Nano doesn’t sit flush on a table, but at 101 grams (0.22 pounds) it’s still really lightweight. [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: I can’t speak for those with bigger hands, but I’d expect the Nano controller won’t be well-suited to everyone. The size makes it ideal for young children, though. I tried to get my 1-year-old son to try the Nano, and he responded with a smile, so I guess he likes it. I haven’t had enough time to get a full idea of battery life yet, but it seems to drain around 10 percent in around 30 to 40 minutes. That suggests a lot less battery life than the 30 hours you’d get on a rechargeable pack for the larger Xbox wireless controller. Thankfully, the Nano charges quickly, and I found I could get from 30 percent to 60 percent charge in less than 10 minutes. You can plug in a USB-C charger to top up the battery and carry on playing while you charge. [Product: Xbox Nano Controller | The only thing missing on the Nano controller that I would have loved is vibration support. I assume it’s not there because of an impact on battery life, because even the smaller Nintendo Joy-Con controllers have rumble support. The Xbox Nano controller will be available on November 4th, priced at $49.99.

articles.title: PlayStation Officially Announces Its First 2026 Black Friday Sale
articles.summary: PlayStation has officially announced its upcoming Black Friday sale — but where are the console deals?
articles.body:
PlayStation has officially announced its upcoming 2026 Black Friday sale. Deals drop on PlayStation Direct at midnight on November 4, with the full sale running until November 30. This marks a significant shift from last year’s strategy, which limited discounts to the week of Black Friday proper.

As for what the deals will actually include? This year’s announcement is pretty slim on the details, simply noting that "you’ll find deep discounts up to 75% off, across thousands of PS5, PS4 and PS VR2 games, expansions, and DLC." You read that right — no mention of consoles, accessories, or even PS Plus memberships.

PlayStation’s 2026 Black Friday Sale Is All About the Games

The announcement offers a sneak peek at what games will go on sale, including some big new releases from 2026. We don't know exactly what the discounts will look like, but you can get a sense of each game by clicking through to IGN's original reviews:

Retailers like Best Buy and Amazon have already started dropping early Black Friday deals, where you’ll find even more discounts on older physical PS5 games like God of War Ragnarok and Ghost of Tsushima. Yes, the discs are a touchy subject , I know.

007 First Light - Collector's Edition (PS5)

LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight (PS5)

It’s no secret that consoles are ridiculously expensive, so one would hope Black Friday would be the rare time you can get around the current MSRP. Unfortunately, it’s not looking good for PS5 deals in 2026.

Sony has traditionally announced a new PS5 game bundle for Black Friday, with last year’s being Fortnite-themed . This year? No mention of a bundle at all.

In 2025, Sony dropped a $100 discount across consoles , which pretty much cancelled out the PS5 price hike from the month before. In fact, last year Sony announced discounts across its entire hardware line, including $20 off DualSense controllers and $100 off the PSVR2.

This year’s announcement doesn’t include any indication of hardware discounts. That doesn’t mean the deals won’t exist, but it does suggest they won't be as good as last year, or perhaps even haven’t been settled on yet.

The one sign of hope? A little asterisk next to some sale dates.

The PlayStation announcement notes that some discounts will end on November 20 and be replaced with new offers. This date lines up with when Sony launched its full console deals last year, so there’s still a chance we see a 'second wave' of PlayStation Black Friday deals that actually includes some hardware.

Individual retailers like Best Buy or Amazon may also drop some kind of console discount, I just wouldn't expect it to be too hefty.

PlayStation 5 Console + Additional DualSense Controller

Not all hope is lost if you’re hoping to get your hands on a current-gen console, especially in the lead-up to perhaps the biggest console-exclusive release of all time. (GTA 6, in case that wasn’t clear.) It just might not be brand new.

Sony is currently offering $40 off refurbished PS5 bundles with DualSense controllers. The bundle starts at $518 for the Digital Edition , while the disc-drive model comes to $568 .

If you're looking for some extra cash to spend on Black Friday, Sony is offering up to $400 to anyone willing to offload their PS5 console and controllers. It seems we’re in full refurb territory, which likely stems from ongoing stock issues amid RAMageddon .

articles.title: The Xbox Nano has a hidden cloud secret
articles.summary: Microsoft’s miniature Xbox controller can connect directly to Xbox Cloud Gaming over Wi-Fi.
articles.body: Microsoft is about to launch its new Xbox Nano controller tomorrow, and the tiny device has a little secret. The Nano can connect directly to Xbox Cloud Gaming over Wi-Fi to improve latency. It’s a feature Microsoft hasn’t officially announced yet, but one I’ve been anticipating since the Xbox Nano leaked earlier this year. The Nano will be able to connect directly to Microsoft’s cloud servers to reduce latency, much like how Google’s Stadia controllers used to work. This new cloud connect feature for the Nano is being privately tested on the new Xbox Cloud Gaming website, and it will require you to pair the controller over Wi-Fi to Microsoft’s Xbox Cloud Gaming servers using the Xbox mobile app. [Image: The new Xbox Cloud Gaming website will let you connect a Nano controller to the cloud. I’m expecting Microsoft to announce this as a preview for the new Xbox Nano controller soon, before it’s fully supported across Xbox Cloud Gaming on the web and on smart TVs. I first started reporting that Microsoft was planning a new controller with Wi-Fi connectivity to reduce Xbox Cloud Gaming latency earlier this year. I’d expect the upcoming Xbox Elite 3 controller will also have the same functionality. Microsoft had also planned to introduce a direct-to-cloud feature on a new Xbox controller, codenamed Sebile, as part of an Xbox Series X refresh console in 2024. The refresh console was canceled, and it’s not clear when we’ll eventually see a new Xbox wireless controller with direct cloud functionality.

articles.title: Sony and Lionsgate Team up For Naruto Movie, Filming to Begin in Spring 2027
articles.summary: Sony and Lionsgate have teamed up for the live-action Naruto movie, which is targeting a spring 2027 start date.
articles.body:
Sony and Lionsgate have teamed up for the live-action Naruto movie, which is targeting a spring 2027 start date.

Sony and Lionsgate have confirmed they will work together on Destin Daniel Cretton's live-action Naruto movie , with Lionsgate handling production and domestic distribution. Sony Pictures will handle international distribution. Lionsgate noted in a statement that Sony is a great partner for this specific project given its experience with anime and manga (Sony owns Crunchyroll, for instance).

“As a longtime fan of Naruto, I’ve always loved that beneath the extraordinary action is a story filled with heart, humor, and humanity," said director Destin Daniel Cretton. "Kishimoto-sensei created a world where unlikely heroes do extraordinary things, and that’s what makes it so special. Lionsgate has been an incredible partner, and I’m thrilled to reunite with the fantastic team at Sony. Together, we’re committed to capturing everything fans love about Naruto while introducing it to a whole new generation. I can’t wait for everyone to see what we’re creating.”

The Naruto movie has officially been greenlit by Lionsgate and is now barreling toward a production start date of spring 2027. As a result, we should hear more news on casting in the coming weeks and months. There's currently no confirmed cast for the film at the moment, but actor Charles Melton was reportedly in talks to play Kakashi back in August. Naruto will likely be one of the hottest projects in Hollywood ahead of its production start, with lots of younger actors likely trying to fight for a spot in the ensemble.

Destin Daniel Cretton just directed Spider-Man: Brand New Day, which grossed over $2.5 billion and became the third-highest-grossing film in history. Naturally, it makes sense that Sony would want to be involved with his next project, and it's likely other people in Hollywood will want to get on board as well. Cretton also did a bang-up job on Marvel's Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings, which has given audiences more confidence in his Naruto movie.

Unfortunately, there isn't much precedent for great live-action adaptations of anime. Dragon Ball infamously got a live-action film known as Dragonball Evolution in 2009. It is genuinely awful and it may have scared Hollywood away from trying to adapt other anime after this. Maybe Naruto will crack the code, though.

articles.title: Indie games are missing launch dates because Steam is backed up
articles.summary: Many indie game developers have recently posted on social media about unexpectedly long approval wait times for their game submissions on Steam, with some of the approvals causing developers to miss their planned launch dates.
articles.body: Many indie game developers have recently posted on social media about unexpectedly long approval wait times for their game submissions on Steam, with some of the approvals causing developers to miss their planned launch dates. For example, Studio Daimon, the team behind an upcoming title called Food Devils, had planned to launch the game in early access today after submitting its build on October 12th. But the game is “still awaiting approval,” according to a post from game director Alfred Kamon. “Even now, we don’t know when Steam will give us the final OK to finally release our game. We sent another ticket last week saying that the situation was urgent and that we might miss our release date because of this, but it also got ignored.” In October, publisher 2 Left Thumbs said it missed its planned launch of Wheel Make It “by nearly two weeks” due to the long wait for build reviews. You can read some details about the studio’s setbacks, including failing a review for a “one single option in the menu” not being accessible with a controller, in a Steam post. There are lots of other recent posts about review build waits as well. Valve says on a Steam developer website that a review of a game’s store presence “typically takes 3-5 business days to complete,” though the company suggests submitting a page for review “at least 7 business days before you want it live to account for potential changes you’ll need to make.” However, as of late, Steam has seemingly been grappling with a sharp increase in games; October’s Steam Next Fest had 7,240 games, a 65.2 percent increase over June’s Steam Next Fest, according to How to Market a Game. A Reddit user also found that 49.9 percent of all games released since Valve started asking developers in 2024 to label games that use AI now have an AI disclosure. Kamon and 2 Left Thumbs suspect the longer waits are due to “slop” slowing down the process. “We can only assume it’s because Steam’s review queue is clogged up by AI slop, but the whole process is now taking several weeks for some developers,” said Kamon. In a new post from Valve published after we first ran this story, the company acknowledged that following a “a significant increase in submissions for store and page review in recent months,” it’s “running a little behind right now” and taking “up to 12 business days” for reviews, saying that much of the delay is “having to re-review games.” It has updated its release checklist for developers, including requiring them to run a game through Steam for at least five minutes. Valve also says that further improvements are on the way for the build review process. Itch.io has also been dealing with a rise in games, with the platform saying last weekend that “The number of game pages being created per-day has doubled in the past 2 months.” Last night, the platform said it “Just deleted a couple terabytes of ai slop 😌” Update, November 3rd: Added new post from Valve.

articles.title: Mason Thames Cast as Robin in DC's Dynamic Duo Movie, DC Studios Boss Says Actor Is 'Obsessed' With the Role
articles.summary: How to Train Your Dragon star Mason Thames has been cast as Dick Grayson/Robin in DC's upcoming Dynamic Duo movie.
articles.body:
How to Train Your Dragon star Mason Thames has been cast as Dick Grayson/Robin in DC's upcoming Dynamic Duo movie.

The news has been rumored for a while, with Thames even teasing it on his socials earlier this year, but has been properly confirmed by DC Studios co-head Peter Safran. When speaking with Collider , Safran confirmed that Thames will play Dick Grayson in the animated film and that the actor aggressively pursued the role.

"We always talk about wanting volunteers and not recruits to be part of the DCU, to be part of DC Studios, and Mason always wanted to be Dick Grayson," said Safran. "He just did. And he came in, and auditioned the s**t out of it, and was awesome. He's a wonderful young actor, but boy, did he want this. He was just obsessed. When he came over to the DC offices, he came over with his dad at the time, and we’ve got tons of great archives and stuff in there, and wanted to take a picture of everything and with everything. He's a fan."

Thames is expected to play the character while he's still Robin, as the film will follow Jason Todd and Dick Grayson in their earliest days . That means you shouldn't expect Nightwing or Red Hood to appear, or perhaps not initially. Dynamic Duo is expected to be a pretty unique film, as it will blend traditional CGI animation with stop motion and puppetry. It's unclear exactly how this will be executed, but the vision must be strong for DC to have greenlit the project. Safran also told Collider a bit about the technology they're using to bring their ideas to life.

9 DC Graphic Novels You Should Read to Understand James Gunn's DCU

"I think that the Swaybox technology is as original today as Pixar was when it did Toy Story," he said. "I really think it's that different from anything that's come before it. Even though it's puppets with an overlay of CGI, the fact that it's shot with real cameras brings a visceral nature to the action in a way that I don't think animation itself ever can really capture. I am really, really excited for people to witness what Arthur [Mintz] and Theresa [Andersson], who are the Swaybox founders, have come up with. I think it's really unusual and cool, and it’s a great way to tell a story."

Not much else is known about the film, and it's not totally clear if the two Robins will have a Batman to mentor them. James Gunn recently stated that the search for the DCU's Batman will begin soon , and they're looking for someone who is around the same age as Superman actor David Corenswet. Gunn had also previously stated when the DCU was just getting started that he expected actors to play their roles across all mediums , including live-action and animation. As a result, whoever gets cast as the next Batman may have a voice role in Dynamic Duo, but that's pure speculation. Similarly, that could also mean Mason Thames may play Nightwing in live-action in the future, as well.

articles.title: Xbox Made an Alligator-Shaped Series X, and You Can Win It Before GTA 6 Launches
articles.summary: GTA 6 is mere weeks away from launch, and to celebrate, Xbox is bringing the wildlife of Leonida to players’ living rooms with a one-of-a-kind console.
articles.body:
GTA 6 is mere weeks away from launch, and to celebrate, Xbox is bringing the wildlife of Leonida to players’ living rooms with a one-of-a-kind console.

The Xbox Series X-Bite, as it’s been affectionately dubbed by the company, is a 5-foot-long, alligator-shaped, fully functional Xbox Series X. It’s quite convincing, actually, and it even looks like a piece of genuine taxidermy. Thankfully, that’s not the case; this life-sized fake alligator was created in partnership with John Nolan Studio, which created special effects for Netflix’s The Witcher series, Jurassic World Dominion , and HBO’s upcoming Harry Potter show.

To turn on the console, simply push the Xbox button on the gator’s back; it’s got a controller placed carefully in its jaws, bearing tooth marks as proof of its ravenous appetite. Even the pupils in its eyes are shaped like an X, outlined in green in keeping with Xbox branding.

This strange blend of technology and artwork isn’t an avante-garde installation sitting in the Microsoft corporate offices; starting today, November 3, fans can enter a sweepstakes to win the quirky console for themselves. Here’s how to participate:

Follow @XBOX on your platform of choice. (X, Instagram, or TikTok) Your profile must be public.

Repost the designated XBOX sweepstakes post.

Manually add #XbiteSweepstakes to your repost.

The sweepstakes lasts until 11:59pm PT on November 10, 2026. The lucky winner will have 48 hours to claim the console; if they fail to do so, the gator will “make a clean getaway.” Additionally, the sweepstakes is only open to legal residents of the 50 U.S. and D.C. who are 18 years of age or older.

While Xbox didn’t directly mention GTA 6 in its posts about this unique contest, it’s hard not to see why it was made; the game takes place in a fictional version of Florida, which, as most folks will know, is home to all sorts of critters, including alligators. (It’s unclear if players will be able to wrassle gators bare-handed like they do in real-life Florida, but we figure the X-Bite is the next best thing.)

GTA 6 launches on November 19 on PS5, PS5 Pro, and Xbox Series X|S. (Or the X-Bite.) Just this morning, its install size and global release times were revealed, with preload dates also confirmed for November 9 and 10.

Given that the file size is 212 GB, Rockstar has urged players to preload the game on their consoles as soon as they can. “Make sure you've got ample space to begin pre-loading as soon as possible,” Rockstar said on the game’s official website.

Fans are more keen than ever to get their hands on a copy of GTA 6, to the point where oodles of IGN’s readers are actually calling out of work to play it . A separate survey from Unwind Media even shared some concerning statistics that showed a baffling amount of players are so desperate to play the game early that they would even give up their pets if that meant they could experience it a week before launch.

articles.title: Ubisoft Among Suitors Trying to Buy Marvel's Blade, Dishonored Studio Arkane Lyon from Xbox
articles.summary: Ubisoft is reportedly among multiple suitors preparing bids to try and purchase French developer Arkane Lyon, makers of the Dishonored series and the upcoming Marvel's Blade, from Microsoft in the wake of the first-party publisher's ongoing Xbox "reset."
articles.body:
Ubisoft is reportedly among multiple suitors preparing bids to try and purchase French developer Arkane Lyon, makers of the Dishonored series and the upcoming Marvel's Blade, from Microsoft in the wake of the first-party publisher's ongoing Xbox " reset ."

According to a new report from Bloomberg, at least three companies have submitted bids to Microsoft so far, with Assassin's Creed publisher Ubisoft among them. The identities of the other bidders are not yet publicly known, but Microsoft has not accepted any bids yet. Bloomberg states that a deal would allow Arkane Lyon to complete its current project, Marvel's Blade, which the outlet says "is expected to be released within the next year or two."

Arkane's other studio in Austin, Texas, was closed by Microsoft in 2024 as part of a larger series of project cuts and personnel layoffs. The Austin team had been responsible for the critically acclaimed studio's only flop, 2023's disappointing co-op vampire-hunting game Redfall, which IGN gave a 4 out of 10 in our review . Previously, Arkane Austin developed the buggy-at-launch-but-quickly-fixed immersive sim Prey as well as the beloved original Dishonored.

Arkane Lyon, meanwhile, was responsible for the 10-out-of-10 first-person immersive sim Deathloop along with the outstanding Dishonored 2.

Four studios have been spun out of Xbox so far rather than being immediately shut down as part of the "reset": Double Fine, which has gone independent ; Compulsion Games, which has also gone independent ; Undead Labs, which has gone independent but signed a publishing deal with an unidentified company for State of Decay 3; and Ninja Theory, which unfortunately might close down after Microsoft had two deals for another company to acquire it fall through .

articles.title: Valve is making changes to deal with a ‘significant increase’ in Steam game submissions
articles.summary: Valve acknowledged that it’s seen “a significant increase in submissions for store and page review in recent months,” is taking “up to 12 business days” for reviews.
articles.body: In a new post today, Valve acknowledged that it’s seen “a significant increase in submissions for store and page review in recent months” and says it’s “running a little behind” by taking “up to 12 business days” for reviews instead of the typical 3-5 days. Indie developers have recently expressed frustrations over lengthy approval times for Steam games, even causing some games to miss planned launch dates. Valve says that “much” of the delay is having to re-review games, so it’s making some changes to the release checklist for developers to hopefully “cut down on re-reviews for basic functional issues.” The changes include requiring developers to run games through Steam for at least five minutes. “Believe it or not, sometimes we review builds that have not ever been played through Steam,” Valve says. “This means that even if a game runs smoothly when a dev launches their executable directly, they might have missed basic steps that would impact a user installing and playing via Steam.” Other requirements include making sure that achievements are ready and confirming any required common redistributables, like DirectX or Visual C++, that Steam may need to install. Valve also says more improvements are in the works for the build review process.

articles.title: 007 First Light Gets Free Trial For Select PlayStation Plus Subscribers
articles.summary: Select PlayStation Plus subscribers can try 007 First Light for free via a new trial.
articles.body:
Select PlayStation Plus subscribers can try 007 First Light for free via a new trial.

007 First Light is one of the biggest games of 2026, but you'd be forgiven for having missed it. It's been a busy year filled with a wide variety of awesome things to play. With the holiday season on the horizon, the game has already started to receive some sizable discounts , so IO Interactive is warming up potential new fans. If you have PlayStation Plus Premium or Deluxe, you can try a 1-hour trial of 007 First Light.

This will allow you to play the game's prologue and some of Bond's training sections, which are actually quite fun and inventive for a video game tutorial. It's a great way to come to grips not only with how the game feels to play, but also the story and IO Interactive's take on Bond. If you like it, you can buy the game for 40% off, which brings it down to about $42.

007 First Light is one of the most well-reviewed games of 2026, with IGN giving it a 9 out of 10 and praising it for being a smart yet faithful evolution of the beloved spy franchise.

"Demonstrably obsessed with bringing the Bond fantasy to life in a way no game has ever managed before, developer IO Interactive has found a highly successful home for the more curated action-stealth formula of 2012’s Hitman: Absolution," reads an excerpt from our review. "Patiently paced, First Light is brimming with Bond’s trinity of gadgets, guns, and girls in a way that feels fresh but reverent, and never like parody."

007 First Light has sold over 4 million copies as of August 2026 and will presumably rack up a few more copies sold throughout the holiday season, especially if it scores some end-of-year awards. IO Interactive has also released some free post-launch updates for the game to encourage players to revisit it and is planning to drop a new story DLC before the end of the year. Next year, Nintendo Switch 2 fans will also have the opportunity to play the game when it is ported over to the console in March.
